sources.title: Perplexity announces Sonar API
sources.evidence: The official Perplexity account introduces Sonar and a separate Pro version. The normal X page was inaccessible; original text, business-verified author and created_at 2025-01-21T19:02:04.000Z were retrieved through the first-party X syndication endpoint cited separately.

sources.title: First-party X syndication data for Sonar launch
sources.evidence: Returns the exact original Perplexity announcement, post identifier, author and January 21, 2025 timestamp. This establishes the named Sonar API launch rather than the release of older llama-3.x-sonar aliases.

sources.title: Perplexity official blog archive
sources.evidence: Direct HTML dates Introducing the Sonar Pro API January 21, 2025 and Meet New Sonar February 11, 2025. The latter is a later model upgrade. Also dates RL training research May 5 and speculative decoding research June 10, 2025.

sources.title: Meet New Sonar
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27 through the complete indexed primary article; direct page access still failed. The February 11, 2025 announcement identifies Sonar as further-trained Llama 3.3 70B, explicitly names Llama 3.3 70B Instruct as its base, and includes Sonar API availability. It describes factuality/readability training, with no target pruning, distillation, expert expansion or added neural modality described. Supports a nominal unchanged language-backbone inference, not a complete later multimodal service count.

sources.title: Meta Llama 3.3 model card
sources.evidence: Freshly read Meta's raw repository card October 27. The exact Llama 3.3 text-only model table publishes nominal 70B parameters and an autoregressive Transformer with grouped-query attention. It does not separately publish active parameters; the active convention is supplied by the original Microsoft and Alem comparison plots, not inferred from dense architecture.

sources.title: Accelerating Sonar through speculation
sources.evidence: Reopened the complete primary article October 27 through its official redirect. The June 10, 2025 research distinguishes Sonar target inference from a separately fine-tuned Llama 1B draft. MTP heads and DeepSeek experiments are discussed separately. The draft is excluded from the target backbone count; this article does not publish a separate active count or complete multimodal total.

sources.title: Perplexity RL training for math reasoning
sources.evidence: Read the indexed first-party research body. Its illustrative GRPO experiments explicitly use Llama 3.1 8B base and instruct models. These are not exact Sonar parameter disclosures and their size or training recipe is not transferred to Sonar. Direct article access was restricted.

sources.title: Retained Sonar model documentation
sources.evidence: Directly retrieved exact Sonar card labels it a non-reasoning model with 128K context and web-search answers with citations. It uses the sonar model identifier. The page is retained for customers with continued Sonar access after the Chat Completions migration, so these are last-documented legacy specifications, not a fresh endpoint test.

sources.title: Perplexity API changelog
sources.evidence: January 2025 announces Sonar/Sonar Pro and separately deprecates older Llama Sonar aliases. April 2025 announces image upload to Sonar; September 2025 announces PDF, DOC, DOCX, TXT and RTF attachment support for Sonar models. Search-depth options and later Pro Search changes are service updates, not independent Sonar releases or parameter disclosures.

sources.title: Sonar now supports image upload
sources.evidence: Direct forum JSON identifies the April 16, 2025 announcement's author as Perplexity forum staff/admin. It explicitly announces images in Sonar API requests for multimodal queries. It does not disclose the visual encoder, preprocessing or model parameter composition.

sources.title: Retained Sonar API request schema
sources.evidence: Exact legacy API schema includes sonar in the model enumeration and text, image_url, file_url and pdf_url message content. It exposes retrieval controls but no tools/tool_choice request fields. The shared schema alone does not prove every listed media capability for every variant or establish model-selected tool use.

sources.title: Retained Sonar media and attachments documentation
sources.evidence: Direct Markdown retrieval documents image/file request handling and retrieved image/video response URLs. Upload examples use sonar-pro, so those examples alone are not treated as base Sonar evidence. Returning web images or videos is retrieval rather than model image/video generation; the Sonar-specific announcements provide the additional base-model input evidence.

sources.title: Retained Pro Search tools documentation
sources.evidence: Describes automatic model selection of built-in web_search and fetch_url_content in Pro Search and excludes custom tool registration. Its scope is Pro Search; it does not establish the base sonar model's tool-selection capabilities.

sources.title: Perplexity API terms, January 23, 2026
sources.evidence: Accessed full terms explicitly covering Sonar and Agentic Research API services. Sections 2.1 and 3.1 grant limited service rights and reserve Perplexity/licensor rights in the services and related models. Supports descriptive Proprietary classification, not an open checkpoint license.

sources.title: Perplexity third-party model terms
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened October 27. The November 25, 2025 legal page calls Sonar a Perplexity-operated Llama 3.1 70B fine-tune. Its base-version label conflicts with the specific February Llama 3.3 upgrade announcement. Both give nominal 70B, but the generic legal page does not establish a later reversion or resolve the current backend.

sources.title: Perplexity official public model inventory
sources.evidence: Queried the official developer inventory; its 27 public repositories contain no Sonar checkpoint. Combined with the hosted release and terms, this supports closed weights. No relevant checkpoint was available for bounded configuration or safetensors-header inspection; no weight shards were downloaded.

sources.title: Sonar to Agent API migration
sources.evidence: Sonar Chat Completions support ended September 27, 2026. Synchronous and streaming calls are gradually reformulated as Agent API requests according to the model; asynchronous calls are unsupported. This does not prove that current Agent API presets retain the legacy Sonar checkpoint or context specification.

sources.title: Agent API model list
sources.evidence: Current model table explicitly lists perplexity/sonar as Perplexity's grounded search model. It cautions that tool and reasoning support vary by model. Continued identity listing does not establish unchanged weights or authorize transferring generic Agent API tools to the legacy Sonar record.

sources.title: Agent API and Sonar benchmark comparison
sources.evidence: Freshly retrieved the full official Markdown October 27. The exact Sonar baseline tables report BrowseComp/DSQA quality and cost, with no total or active parameter column. The page identifies these as pre-retirement Sonar baselines and maps Sonar to Agent API fast effort. It does not establish that the replacement preserves the documented 2025 backbone.

sources.title: Phi-4: Microsoft Research January 2025 brief, page 1
sources.evidence: Reopened the original two-page PDF and visually inspected page 1 on October 27. Its MMLU-pro comparison chart explicitly labels the horizontal axis Active Parameters (Billions), with the exact Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct point at approximately 70B. This is Microsoft's published nominal research-comparison convention for the named Sonar base, not Meta or Perplexity's own active-count disclosure and not an exact per-token tensor census.

sources.title: Benchmarking Open-Ended Multi-Agent Coordination in Language Agents, Figure 11
sources.publisher: Kale-ab Abebe Tessera et al.; University of Edinburgh, University of Oxford and University College London
sources.evidence: Reopened the original June 2026 paper October 27 and visually inspected Figure 11 on PDF page 24. Its explicitly labeled Active parameters (billions, log scale) axis places Llama 3.3 70B at approximately 70B. Section 4.1 and Table 1 identify the evaluated model as Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, served with vLLM. This corroborates the original researchers' nominal active convention for the exact named base; plot precision does not establish exact per-token participation or Sonar's later service composition.

name.note: Exact base Sonar identity; separate from Sonar Pro, Sonar Reasoning and old Llama-prefixed aliases.

developer.note: Perplexity develops the Sonar fine-tune and hosted search service; Meta's base-model authorship is recorded separately.

family.note: Explicit Sonar API family, normalized lowercase; grouping does not imply identical sibling weights.

release_date.note: Original named Sonar API launch, confirmed by the official announcement timestamp. Older Llama Sonar aliases are distinct. February 11 is a later Sonar model upgrade, and image/file support and Agent API migration are subsequent service changes.

open_weights.note: Hosted Perplexity fine-tune with no released Sonar checkpoint in the accessed developer materials and public inventory. Its open-weight Llama ancestor does not make Sonar's trained weights public.

license.note: Descriptive hosted-model/service classification under Perplexity API terms. Underlying third-party license obligations remain separate.

parameters_b.note: Nominal 70B for the language backbone disclosed in the February 2025 Sonar upgrade, retained through Perplexity's explicit further-training relationship to Llama 3.3 70B Instruct. No structural target change is described in that release. Scope is language_backbone; the separate 1B speculative draft and later undisclosed visual/service components are excluded. The legal page's Llama 3.1 label leaves later revision identity unresolved.

active_parameters_b.note: Approximately 70B under the explicit active-parameter plotting conventions of Microsoft Research and Tessera et al. for Llama 3.3 70B Instruct, inherited as a labeled nominal inference for Sonar's documented further-trained language backbone. This is not a direct Perplexity active-count disclosure or a dense-equals-active calculation. The source plots do not establish exact per-token tensor participation; the separate 1B draft, later visual components and replacement Agent API backend are outside scope.

architecture.note: Autoregressive Transformer language backbone, supported by explicit Llama ancestry and later Sonar inference research. This does not identify the later image-processing topology, retrieval system architecture or unchanged current Agent API backend. DeepSeek MoE examples are not Sonar evidence.

context_window.note: 128K is the exact model's last-documented legacy context, normalized to 128,000 tokens. No endpoint request was made; current Agent API preset limits are not substituted.

modalities.note: Documents accepted Sonar API input formats: image support announced April 2025 and PDF/file support September 2025. PDF is a service input format and may be preprocessed; native visual/document encoder details are undisclosed. Pro-only examples and shared video schema are insufficient for extra claims. Returned web-media URLs are not generated image/video modalities.

reasoning.note: Exact card explicitly classifies legacy Sonar as non-reasoning. This denotes the dedicated reasoning-model mode, not an inability to reason; no sibling or generic Agent API mode is inherited.

tool_call.note: Built-in retrieval does not establish model-selected tool calls. The exact legacy request surface lacks custom-tool fields, while automatic built-in tool selection is documented for Pro Search. Neither establishes a blanket true/false capability for base Sonar; current generic Agent API tools are not transferred.

description.value: Perplexity search model that generates answers with web citations and accepts text, image and document inputs.
description.note: Plain description of documented hosted capabilities; avoids unsupported speed/quality claims and does not describe current Agent API presets as the original model.

patch.description: Perplexity search model that generates answers with web citations and accepts text, image and document inputs.
patch.notes: The February 2025 Sonar language backbone has nominal 70B total parameters through explicit Llama 3.3 70B Instruct further-training lineage. Approximately 70B active is inherited from Microsoft Research and Tessera et al. comparison plots for that base, not directly disclosed by Perplexity. Both counts exclude the separate 1B speculative draft and undisclosed visual/service components. A later legal page names Llama 3.1; later backend identity remains unresolved. Image/PDF are API inputs, and context/non-reasoning are retained legacy specifications. Sonar Chat Completions support ended September 27, 2026; requests are gradually reformulated into Agent API calls. Current model listing does not prove unchanged weights or tools.

summary: Fresh October 27 parameter re-audit retained nominal 70B total and established approximately 70B active for the February 2025 language backbone through explicit Perplexity further-training lineage and original Microsoft/Alem active-count plots. Reopened the announcement, Meta card, speculation research, legal terms, legacy card and current migration/comparison documentation; bounded searches for total/active counts and structural changes found no stronger exact Sonar disclosure. Both counts require language_backbone scope. The separate draft, later visual components and current replacement backend remain outside that count. Preserved the other 12 assessments.
